source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.3 'The frame'; 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' the dashboard (p1) masthead block and the account/settings (p14/p15) mastheads (identical shape, different eyebrow suffix and command-bar placeholder); operator rulings 2.3 (no second ask bar) and 5.1/5.2 (the masthead card's own top rule)
notes: Masthead.tsx is a pure-inline-style component (no Tailwind utility classes), so every property below is a real product value, not a harness artefact.

Command bar border: the artboard states `border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25)` on the search bar; CommandBar.tsx uses `var(--line-1)` = rgba(0,0,0,.12) (theme.css). A real token-vs-artboard gap, not a harness artefact.

UI FIX ROUND 2026-09-08, item A1 (lane cardrule). This note used to read that 'the masthead CARD ITSELF carries no background/border/radius/shadow/top-rule of its own in Masthead.tsx', recording a real gap between the shared part and dc.html p1, which wraps the masthead content in the same white radius-10 card shell every panel gets with the 3px dark-grey graduated rule as its first child. The operator's item A1 names 'the masthead card' among the eighteen card types missing the rule, so the gap is closed: Masthead.tsx now renders `SectionCard` as its root, and the two rows below measure the shell and the rule on the shared part itself.

children.name: title (list size, 34px)
children.note: dc.html p1: font-family Anton, text-transform uppercase, letter-spacing .04em, font-size 34px, line-height 1.08. Masthead.tsx sets line-height 1.05 (its own documented choice for both sizes), not stated by the artboard as a divergence — logged as a note, not asserted, to avoid a false MISMATCH on a value the artboard doesn't actually contrast against a differing built intent.

children.name: command bar — outer form
children.note: dc.html p1: height 40px, border 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25), border-radius 8px, background #fff.

children.name: command bar — input font size
children.note: dc.html p1: the search text is 13px. The artboard's #7A6E6C colour paints the PLACEHOLDER glyph in its static markup (there is no typed-vs-placeholder distinction in a static mock); this input's inline `color` governs text the reader TYPES, which the product correctly renders in ink for legibility, so colour is not asserted here (asserting it would compare the wrong thing, not a real design statement about typed-text colour).

children.name: command bar — placeholder text (default, item-count form)
children.note: UPDATED, CMDSEARCH lane, 2026-09-09, reason not weakness: the operator's own instruction ("a toggel between standard search and AI question in that bar") split the bar into an explicit Search/Ask mode toggle, so the DEFAULT (Search-mode) placeholder no longer needs the words "or ask" to carry that meaning — the toggle itself now shows it at a glance. Prior text 'Search or ask across 1,434 items…'; CommandBar still formats the count with the app's own thousands separator, unchanged. Read via the `placeholder` DOM property (an input's textContent is always empty).

children.name: command bar — ⌘K hint
children.note: dc.html p1: font-size 10px, font-family ui-monospace/monospace, color #7A6E6C, padding 0 10px.

children.name: command bar — submit button
children.note: SELECTOR NARROWED, CMDSEARCH lane, 2026-09-09, reason not weakness: the bar's new Search/Ask mode toggle (operator instruction, same lane) adds two more `<button>`s inside `.cl-command-bar`, so the bare tag selector `.cl-command-bar button` now matches the FIRST button in DOM order (a toggle tab, not the submit button) and reads its style instead. The submit button already carried no distinguishing class; `.cl-command-bar-ask-submit` is added to it so this row addresses the SAME element the artboard means, unambiguously, rather than whichever button happens to come first. dc.html p1: height 100% (=40px, the bar's own height), padding 0 14px, background #5A5552, color #fff, font-size 12.5px, font-weight 700. CommandBar.tsx builds the button at a fixed 30px height inside the 40px bar (not the full-height artboard treatment) and padding 0 16px. Geometry is UNCHANGED by SEARCHFIX (2026-09-11) below — only the row's own name and its label expectation move, because this row's real subject is a label, not the box.

children.name: command bar — submit button label
children.note: SELECTOR NARROWED, CMDSEARCH lane, 2026-09-09 — see the row above for why. UPDATED, SEARCHFIX, 2026-09-11, reason not weakness: operator report (verbatim, "i hit ask and nothing happens when trying standard search") traced to this control being hard-wired to the literal text "Ask" and to `ask()` regardless of the active mode — pressing it in Search mode (the bar's DEFAULT mode, `useState("search")`) silently asked the assistant, or did nothing visible when the assistant was disabled, instead of running a search. The control now reads what it does in the mode it is in: "Search" in Search mode, "Ask" in Ask mode (src/components/ui/CommandBar.tsx, `{mode === "ask" ? "Ask" : "Search"}`). This row asserts the label at REST — the mounted, un-toggled state — which is Search mode's "Search", not the dc.html artboard's single static "Ask" capture (the artboard predates the mode toggle entirely; CMDSEARCH's own row-89 note already documents the toggle as this lane's addition, not the artboard's). This is a label fix, not a weakening: the row still asserts an exact string every render must match, only the string is now correct for what ships.

children.name: A1: the masthead card carries the 3px graduated rule as its first child
children.note: Operator item A1 (2026-09-08). The exact gradient is asserted, not just a 3px height.

children.name: A3: the masthead card's own shell (shadow, 1px rgba(0,0,0,.12) border, radius 10)
children.note: Operator item A3 (2026-09-08), supplied by SectionCard rather than by this caller.
